description.plain:
Business Problem

Cement plants depend on reliable equipment and timely availability of maintenance spares. Maintenance orders, breakdown notifications, cost postings, equipment attributes, preventive-maintenance plans and material/stock information may sit in separate operational domains. Without a consolidated view, teams can find it difficult to identify the plant or equipment driving downtime, understand maintenance-cost exposure, monitor PM-related breakdown patterns and check whether critical spares are available against reorder parameters.

description.plain:
Three Key Business Questions

Which plants, equipment categories and assets are contributing most to breakdowns, downtime and production volume loss?

Are equipment reliability and maintenance costs visible at plant and equipment level, and which areas require management attention?

Which MRO materials are close to or below reorder parameters, and how does the recorded PM compliance status relate to breakdown events?

description.plain:
CARD 3

KPIs & Definitions

Six headline KPIs from the supplied dashboard, with formula and evidence notes

The values below reproduce the displayed dashboard and are cross-checked against FINAL_SAC_FACT where the workbook contains the required inputs. KPI targets are not specified in the supplied PDF or workbook and must be approved by the business owner.

Figure 4. KPI-card strip from Maintenance Head’s Cockpit (PDF page 2).

Figure 5. KPI-card strip from Store Head’s Cockpit (PDF page 3).

KPI — Dashboard Value — Formula / Definition

Fleet Availability — 99.28% — MTBF ÷ (MTBF + MTTR) × 100. Current model assumes 100 equipment × 8,760 scheduled hours less recorded downtime.

MTBF (Hours) — 822.79 h — (100 × 8,760 − 6,311 downtime hours) ÷ 1,057 breakdown events. Do not average row-level MTBF.

MTTR (Hours) — 5.97 h — Total Downtime Hours ÷ Breakdown Count = 6,311 ÷ 1,057.

Production Volume Loss — 859,142 tons — SUM(Downtime Hours × Planned Hourly Output Tons), calculated at order/event row before aggregation.

Maintenance Cost — ₹1.38 crore on page 2; ₹27.52 lakh on page 3 — SUM(Maintenance_Cost) from the maintenance-order fact. Page-level dashboard values conflict; confirm filters/calculation scope and formatting.

Total Inventory Value — ₹97.18 crore displayed — Governed definition should sum one snapshot per distinct Material + Plant. Workbook stock snapshot = about ₹11.72 crore; flat order-row sum overstates the value.

Supporting Metrics & Interpretation

Average Cost per Breakdown Event = SUM(Maintenance_Cost) ÷ SUM(Breakdown Count) = ₹13,072.47 in the workbook and Store Head’s Cockpit. Breakdown Count totals 1,057 events. The PM-status chart attributes these breakdown events as 67.46% Completed On Time, 23.18% Completed Late and 9.37% Missed; this is a breakdown distribution by the attached PM status, not a standalone PM completion-rate KPI.

description.plain:
Data Architecture

Layer — Role — Content

SAP S/4HANA – Source System — Operational source — Orders, notifications, equipment, locations, materials, MRP/stock, PM plans, movements, costs and plant/cost-centre data.

SAP Datasphere – Data Layer — Integration and modelling — Staging, key alignment, cost/movement pre-aggregation, inventory snapshot grain and governed views.

SAP Analytics Cloud — Analytics and presentation — FINAL_SAC_FACT import model; three cockpit pages, calculations, filters and audit tables.

description.plain:
Key Dashboard Insights

Area — Dashboard Observation — Evidence / Note

Reliability — Fleet availability is displayed at 99.28%; MTBF is 822.79 hours and MTTR is 5.97 hours. — Maintenance Head’s Cockpit, PDF p.2; FINAL_SAC_FACT calculations.

Breakdown and downtime — The workbook contains 1,057 breakdown events and 6,311 downtime hours. Production Volume Loss is 859,142 tons. — FINAL_SAC_FACT; PDF pp.2–3.

Maintenance spend — The workbook order-cost total is ₹13,817,602.98 (about ₹1.38 crore). The PDF shows ₹1.38 crore on page 2 but ₹27.52 lakh on page 3. — FINAL_SAC_FACT / COEP_Costs reconciliation; PDF pp.2–3. Reconcile page filters/logic.

MRO inventory — The Store Cockpit displays ₹97.18 crore. Distinct Material + Plant stock snapshot records (180 pairs) total about ₹11.72 crore; the row-sum on the flattened order fact duplicates snapshots. — MARD_MBEW_Stock and FINAL_SAC_FACT. Correct the inventory grain before certifying the KPI.

PM status association — Breakdown events by attached PM status: Completed On Time 67.46%; Completed Late 23.18%; Missed 9.37%. — FINAL_SAC_FACT. This is breakdown distribution by plan status, not the PM compliance rate.

Average event cost — Average Cost per Breakdown Event is ₹13,072.47 (maintenance cost ÷ breakdown count). — FINAL_SAC_FACT; matches Store Head’s Cockpit.
